prototype.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: visual development paintover for a realtime s&box game environment; a concrete hydroelectric spillway, realistic modern game art.
Input image: edit target, the existing game screenshot. Preserve the exact camera, dam architecture, four waterfall positions and widths, buildings, mountains, sky, lighting, signage, gameplay layout and all foreground objects.
Primary request: redesign ONLY the water flowing down the four large spillways and the associated foam and spray at their foot. The existing water looks like flat blue-grey translucent striped curtains. Replace it with convincing massive fast moving water running down a sloping dam face. Match the level of a detailed realistic contemporary game.
Water art direction: coherent heavy silver-white aerated torrents, darker desaturated teal folds just below each crest, irregular descending streams merging and breaking up, varied widths and densities across each sheet, broad cloudy white turbulence under fine sharply resolved droplet filaments. Increasing aeration and broken froth toward the bottom. Natural asymmetry and ragged edges; no identical lanes. Water has body and daylight shading instead of looking like a self-lit texture.
At the foot: localized low clouds of soft mist rising from each impact, layered semi-transparent spray and dense churning pale foam spreading a short distance into the tailrace. Leave architecture readable. Keep mist restrained and plausible.
Style: detailed photorealistic game screenshot paintover, instantaneous fast shutter water detail rather than long exposure silky streaks. The falls should read well from this camera distance.
Constraints: change only waterfalls and their immediate impact water/mist. Keep all architecture and the rest of the screenshot stable. No HUD, extra structures, text labels, glowing blue water, zebra stripes, repetitive sine waves, rectangular texture boundaries, painting brush strokes, cinematic color grade, or exaggerated fog.

texture.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: production realtime VFX texture, a single tileable grayscale whitewater turbulence density map for a large hydroelectric waterfall shader.
Create a square 2048 by 2048 texture filling the whole frame with detailed irregular aerated water and foam. Water travels vertically from top toward bottom. Dense three-dimensional-looking clumps of white turbulent froth break into fine white droplet filaments and narrow branching streams, with dark cavities and dark flowing water between clumps. Mix broad 100-300 pixel billows, intermediate torn ribbons and crisp very fine 2-12 pixel foam detail. Organically varied density, substantial readable mid-greys as well as whites and blacks. Coherent flowing shapes rather than static marble or cotton clouds. Photographic high-speed water microstructure translated into a neutral greyscale density pattern.
This is a flat material map: no perspective, no background scene, no dam, no rocks, no horizon, no border, no labels, no text, no illumination gradient, no coloured light, no objects. Seamless tile on all four edges; patterns continue naturally across edges. No straight stripes, no repeated parallel waves, no long-exposure silky blur, no even dots, no obvious grid, no glossy highlights or baked cast shadows. Black means water without bubbles; white means dense aeration. Opaque background.
